answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint: distribute the Constructorizer and two Facturers across three separate level-0 Base Cores. Heavy-machine heat is 500/650/650, leaving 500/350/350 capacity before supporting loads. No two heavy machines may share a core. Construction remains gated on verifying Update 1 availability and confirming each core’s complete projected load does not exceed 1,000.

claims.value: The recovered parent architecture is a proposed, not-yet-built Update 1 backbone-and-spurs network with a protected hub, distributed production cells, single-item lines and buffers, and measured rail upgrades; it replaced the superseded monolithic mega-base plan because level-0 Base Core capacity constrains density.

The new explicit player requirement is one Constructorizer plus two Facturers while every Base Core stays level 0 and every occupied core retains Fire Wave protection. Using the authoritative saved values, the machines contribute 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 heat. A level-0 core has 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables protection; Constructorizer-plus-Facturer is 1,150, two Facturers are 1,300, and all three are 1,800, so every possible heavy-machine co-location is unsafe and rejected.

The safe revised layout uses three distinct occupied level-0 Base Cores: Core A hosts only the Constructorizer at 500 heat, leaving 500 capacity; Cores B and C each host only one Facturer at 650 heat, leaving 350 capacity apiece. Those balances are before generators, processors, storage, drone stations, or other supporting buildings, so each support load must be charged to its actual core and kept within that core’s remaining capacity. Preserve the distributed rail backbone; Update 1 rails v.1-v.3 conduct power at zero power draw, but this does not authorize uncounted powered support equipment or disputed amplifier capacity.

Before construction, inspect the live Update 1 build and recipe menus to confirm the Constructorizer, Facturer, required recipes, power sources, and supporting components are actually available; hidden, future, pre-Update-1, and level-10–15 possibly future content remains unauthorized. Then prepare a per-core ledger including every powered building and build one core-machine cell at a time only when its complete projected load is at most 1,000 with deliberate operating margin. Do not credit Base Core Amplifiers until their conflicting capacity values are verified in-game, and stop if any revised load would exceed the threshold.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, artifacts, computations, checkpoints, and next actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, and advance complex work with source fidelity; it is not primarily a notes, transcript, or retrieval product.

The token result must distinguish cumulative cached replay from uncached input: replayed context may contribute to cumulative accounting but is not equivalent to newly supplied uncached model input, so both measures must be reported separately. The process-per-operation BM25 shell and one-shot BM25 results remain regression baselines/fixtures, not the persistent target architecture or product acceptance gate.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace API that reopens a revision-N parent checkpoint, refreshes it to N+1 with an exposed evidence/constraint diff, supports batched typed query/read operations combining exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable child checkpoint containing its parent reference and preserved source references without reconstructing the full prior corpus.

The transition gate passes only when each case completes in no more than four workspace calls, produces answer claims matching the direct-filesystem answer, exposes the N-to-N+1 diff, commits an immutable parent-linked child checkpoint with source lineage, avoids full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer—not primarily a notes app, retrieval system, or memory database. It preserves durable knowledge together with the live goals, evidence, decisions, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, checkpoints, and next actions needed to resume and advance work; Markdown and Obsidian are projections and export formats, not the canonical product boundary.

Cumulative cached replay and uncached input are distinct measurements and must be reported separately; cached replay must not be conflated with newly supplied input or combined into one token figure for comparison with BM25. The frozen regression baseline is policy 0.2: the workspace scored 17/20 cases and 46/53 evidence items at 2,932 mean estimated tokens, while one-shot BM25 top-k scored 17/20 and 48/53 at approximately 1,070 mean estimated tokens. The BM25 shell is only a regression fixture, not the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is a durable snapshot-pinned workspace that reopens a named parent checkpoint at revision N, explicitly refreshes to N+1 with a source-bearing diff, supports typed batched query/read using exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path with explicit degraded fallback, and atomically commits an immutable child checkpoint containing its parent and source lineage. It must reuse the checkpoint and delta when sufficient instead of reconstructing the prior corpus.

The transition passes only when a fresh-agent case completes in at most four successful workspace calls, matches every direct-filesystem answer claim with source citations, exposes the revision-N-to-N+1 change, creates exactly one immutable child linked to its parent with preserved source references, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input. The BM25 result remains the regression baseline rather than the acceptance target.
